title: Unmasking LinkedIn's Hidden Apply Button: 0 to 20 Links | vitalii.no
description:
How a job-pipeline scraper stopped throwing away 643 out of every 644 LinkedIn postings it saw, once it learned LinkedIn had quietly changed its apply button months earlier.

Every LinkedIn row in my job pipeline was getting labeled linkedin_easy_apply and dropped, because the scraper looked for an apply-button link that LinkedIn stopped rendering for anonymous guests months ago. Over 30 days, 643 of 644 postings were thrown in the trash without anyone finding out most of them actually had a normal application form waiting behind an employer's own site.

worker/linkedin_guest.py now parses LinkedIn's public guest page directly, reading its own offsite/onsite apply-link marker to tell an employer-hosted form from a true Easy Apply post, pulling any URL already sitting in the description, and falling back to the employer's company page when nothing else is there. ats_resolver.py runs a keyless cascade before touching any paid search API: posting text, then the guest-page marker, then the employer's website, careers page, and a title match — only falling through to paid search as a last resort, and only counting a hit on the employer's own domain or a known ATS.

Measured on 30 live postings: 20 had a real employer form, 3 were genuine Easy Apply, and 7 were already closed — links that used to be unusable in 643 of 644 cases now mostly resolve, and the rest are honestly classified instead of silently discarded.
